paragraphs.en: If you want to develop {maximum} credibility ( (可信性) ), is it better to be a hedgehog ( (刺猬) ) or a {fox} ? The age-old {idiom} “The fox knows many things, but the hedgehog knows one big thing,”offers a framework for understanding the two approaches to thinking.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你想建立起 <u> 最大的 </u> 可信度，做一只刺猬好呢，还是做一只 <u> 狐狸 </u> 好？有句古老的 <u> 谚 </u> <u> 语 </u> 说：“狐狸知道很多事，但刺猬知道一件大事。”这为我们理解两种思维方式提供了一个框架。

paragraphs.en: Is there a {clear} advantage of one style over the other? Hedgehog thinkers tend to answer {yes} .They are like a {king} in his {castle} , solely focused on ruling his domain.Their thoughts are strong and unyielding, much like {iron} or {steel} .They come down {squarely} on one side or the other and {fully} support their position.And they are usually very {credible} in doing so.According to Jim Collins, the “hedgehog concept” is one of the factors that lead {companies} to greatness.They {concentrate} on one thing and do it really well.They figure out what they are good at.Hence, they have the advantage of {clarity} and {persuade} others more confidently.The hedgehog concept makes perfect sense for companies.
paragraphs.cn: 一种思维方式是否 <u> 明显 </u> 优于另一种呢？拥有刺猬式思维的人往往给出 <u> 肯定的 </u> 答案。他们就像 <u> 城堡 </u> 里的 <u> 国王 </u> ，只专注于统治自己的领地。他们的思想坚定且毫不动摇，就像 <u> 钢铁 </u> 一样。他们会 <u> 明确地 </u> 选择一方或另一方， <u> 完全 </u> 支持自己的立场。他们这样做通常是非常 <u> 可信的 </u> 。吉姆·柯林斯认为，“刺猬理念”是 <u> 公司 </u> 走向卓越的因素之一。这些公司 <u> 专注 </u> 于一件事，并将其做得非常出色。它们清楚自己的擅长之处。因此，它们具有 <u> 思路清晰 </u> 这一优势，并能更加自信地 <u> 说服 </u> 他人。对于公司而言，刺猬理念完全行得通。

paragraphs.en: But there can be a {downside} to concentration on one big thing.Philip Tate has studied the track {records} of those {folks} on the {Sunday} talk shows who make {predictions} about what will happen.He has found that hedgehogs are not only wrong more often than foxes, but that they are less likely to recognize or {admit} that they are wrong when events do not {match} their predictions.Hedgehog thinkers may become blind to alternative perspectives, viewing them as distractions or even {enemies} .
paragraphs.cn: 但是，只专注于一件大事可能会有 <u> 弊端 </u> 。菲利普·泰特研究了那些在 <u> 周日 </u> 脱口秀节目中 <u> 预测 </u> 未来走向的 <u> 人 </u> 的过往 <u> 记录 </u> 。他发现，“刺猬型”的人不仅比“狐狸型”的人更容易犯错，而且当事件与他们的预测不 <u> 符 </u> 时，他们也不太可能认识到或 <u> 承认 </u> 自己的错误。拥有刺猬式思维的人可能会对不同的观点视而不见，将其视为干扰，甚至是 <u> 敌人 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: Fox thinkers are like {journalists} with a {notebook} full of varied stories or a flying {kite} dancing with the changing winds.They seek out new information from a {broader range} of sources, and are comfortable with {uncertainty} and new information.When something is {contradictory} to their view, they don't {treat} it as {exceptional} .They try to include it in their {viewpoint} rather than to {exclude} it from their thinking.They also have a clearer {estimation} of what they know and don't know.However, their {pool} of knowledge can be wide but too shallow to {dive} deep into.Hence, they might not be able to uncover the {missing} {diamond} of wisdom that comes from deep exploration.
paragraphs.cn: 拥有狐狸式思维的人就像 <u> 笔记本 </u> 里装满了各种故事的 <u> 记者 </u> ，也像随着风向变幻而舞动的 <u> 风筝 </u> 。他们从更 <u> 广泛的 </u> 来源寻找新信息，并且能够坦然面对 <u> 不确定性 </u> 和新信息。当某些事情与他们的观点相 <u> 矛盾 </u> 时，他们不会 <u> 将 </u> 其 <u> 视为异常 </u> 。他们会试图将其纳入自己的 <u> 观点 </u> ，而不是将其 <u> 排除 </u> 在思考之外。他们还对自己所知的和不知道的事情有更清晰的 <u> 评估 </u> 。不过，他们的知识 <u> 储备 </u> 可能很广，但太浅，难以深入钻研。因此，他们可能无法从深度探索中发现那块 <u> 丢失的 </u> 智慧之 <u> 钻 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: So, which is better? The question can be answered in a {foxy} hedgehog style.In other words, there are clear advantages for each.The choice between being a hedgehog or a fox is a false {trade-off} .The most {effective} way to go through life is to try to be that {rare} {mixture} known as a foxy hedgehog, who creates a unique {identity} in the {realm} of {autonomous} thinking.
paragraphs.cn: 那么，哪种更好呢？这个问题可以用一种“ <u> 狐狸型 </u> 刺猬”式的思维方式来回答。换句话说，每种思维方式都有其明确的优势。选择做一只刺猬还是一只狐狸其实是一种错误的 <u> 权衡 </u> 。度过人生最 <u> 有效的 </u> 方式是努力成为那种 <u> 稀有的混合体 </u> ，也就是所谓的“狐狸型刺猬”，这类人在 <u> 自主 </u> 思考的 <u> 领域 </u> 创造出了独特的 <u> 身份 </u> 。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
